question: In how many ways can \(10001\) be written as the sum of two primes?
solution:
Two odd numbers have an even sum, as do two even numbers. Since \(10001\) is odd, a prime pair summing to it must contain one even prime and one odd prime.

The only even prime is \(2\): every larger even number has \(2\) as a factor besides \(1\) and itself. Thus the other prime would have to be
\[
10001-2=9999.
\]
But the digits of \(9999\) sum to \(36\), so \(9999\) is divisible by \(3\). Since it is greater than \(3\), it is composite. The only possible pair therefore fails, leaving \(\boxed{0}\) ways, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
